$comment: Contract Verification Results SEP (draft) — the error envelope. THE ONE DOCUMENT HERE THAT IS NOT CLOSED FOR A PRODUCER, deliberately: the others carry claims a consumer parses, and closing them is what makes a version mean something. An error body carries one parsed field (`error`) and one human one (`message`); everything else is diagnostic, and forbidding it would delete operator-facing detail to buy a consistency no consumer asked for.
title: Contract Verification Error (Results SEP 1.0)
description: The body of every non-2xx response on a verifier's or an aggregator's API. One shape across every route, so a client that has learned to read one failure has learned them all.

schema.description: The document type. Every Results SEP document names its type here beside its version.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR of this envelope, versioned independently of the API.

error.description: A stable, machine-readable code. Clients branch on THIS rather than on `message`, and MUST tolerate codes they do not recognise — a verifier adding a code is not a breaking change, and a client that treats it as one fails on every deployment ahead of it. One vocabulary is closed, and it is closed per STATUS rather than per route: the per-hash read route's `400` is exactly `400_invalid_wasm_hash` | `400_other`. That route's other statuses, and every other route, draw from the verifier's failure taxonomy plus `not_found`, `storage_unavailable`, `invalid_request` and `rate_limited`.

message.description: Human-readable. Wording is not stable and is intended for display and debugging — never for a client to branch on.

status_code.description: Implementation detail, not part of this contract: it repeats the HTTP status line. Named here because our deployment sends it and a reader of this schema should not have to wonder whether it means something. The per-hash read routes deliberately omit it.

detail.description: Implementation detail: a longer human-readable form, where a route has one. Not a second machine-readable field.

reason.description: Implementation detail: a sub-code on the one arm that has one (preflight). A client that needs to branch uses `error`.
